findings.where: First screen (desktop and phone), and the whole page: the contact action and the address strip
findings.fault: The page has no way to contact Mark. No email link, contact button or shown address appears anywhere, and the parts map lists nothing that acts except the logo, three nav links, one download link and the replay button. The nav has no Contact item either. The tile's own notes promise an 'address strip' in pad yellow at 'the foot of the sheet', but it was never built. On the first screen the visitor can only read or leave.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank or agency officer who has just read Mark's line and wants to reach him finds no address and no action. They would have to search for him elsewhere. The founder would object too, because the brief requires one direct, personal way to reach Mark, with the address shown, on the first screen.

findings.where: Article specimen, Download list: 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge'
findings.fault: The download looks like a working link to a PDF: blue, underlined and labelled 'PDF'. But it points to '#', so clicking it does nothing and no file opens. The research names the PDF list as the product.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants Mark's lecture clicks and gets nothing. That makes the site look broken and unmaintained.

findings.fault: This is a button that does something on the page, but it is styled as a blue underlined link. The underline is reserved for links. A reader expects it to take them somewhere, but it replays an animation where they are.
findings.who_objects: The founder or Mark, reviewing the tile, may expect it to open a page. Few would be misled for long, since the label is a verb.

findings.fault: Only the yellow swatch has a 2 px blue edge, which looks like a selected or focused tile in a picker. Nothing on it can be clicked. The blue edge is the page's own focus look, so it borrows a state signifier.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the palette may think the yellow swatch is chosen or clickable, and wonder what the selection means.
